subject: series
synopsis: Makoto Ojiro's gentle romance: two insomniac high schoolers find refuge in their school's abandoned observatory and rebuild the astronomy club.

subject: series
synopsis: Gilbert Hernandez's 2000s solo comic following Luba and her sprawling family after Palomar, frank about sex and family life.

subject: series
synopsis: A crossover miniseries uniting the heroes of Marvel's 2099 imprint — Spider-Man 2099, X-Men 2099, Doom 2099, and others — for a shared climactic threat to their dystopian future world.
author: Ben Raab

subject: series
synopsis: Akane Tamura's shojo romance about a girl who always sees herself as a background character, until she falls in love.
author: Akane Tamura

subject: series
synopsis: Annual special issues from AC Comics featuring extended stories with the FemForce and other AC Comics characters, typically showcasing the publisher's golden age revival and female superhero content.
author: Bill Black, Gardner Fox

subject: series
synopsis: The conclusion of the classic Dark Horse Aliens trilogy (originally published by Dark Horse, reprinted by Marvel), following Newt as she leads a desperate mission to the Alien homeworld in a large-scale sci-fi war story.
author: Mark Verheiden

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's post-Secret Wars Avengers lineup features a generationally diverse roster including the new Thor (Jane Foster), Sam Wilson as Captain America, and the teenage Ms. Marvel, Nova, and Miles Morales, exploring legacy, mentorship, and what it means to be an Avenger.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: A short-lived series by Derek Landy featuring the Avengers in high-octane standalone action stories that drop readers into the middle of the action, with each issue self-contained and ending in media res.
author: Derek Landy

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely's definitive Superman story, told as a twelve-chapter mythic farewell: a dying Superman completes twelve legendary labors before his death, reasserting what the character means at the highest possible level. Quitely's luminous, monumental art matches Morrison's ambition at every turn.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology series collecting short stories featuring Spider-Man and his extended cast of allies, enemies, and supporting characters, providing extra content for fans of the web-slinger beyond the main title.
author: Tom DeFalco, J. M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: A tie-in to Annihilation: Conquest following Phyla-Vell as the new Quasar battling the Phalanx technarch invasion; part of the acclaimed cosmic Marvel renaissance that set up the Guardians of the Galaxy relaunch.
author: Christos Gage

subject: series
synopsis: A key Annihilation: Conquest tie-in following Peter Quill leading a ragtag commando unit against the Phalanx -- the series that directly led to the formation of the modern Guardians of the Galaxy.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: An Annihilation: Conquest tie-in introducing the mysterious Wraith, a Kree warrior with unique powers, fighting the Phalanx invasion; atmospheric if somewhat peripheral to the main event.
author: Javier Grillo-Marxuach

subject: series
synopsis: William Messner-Loebs's limited series following Artemis after her resurrection, navigating the underworld and seeking her place in the world of the living. A character study for the second Wonder Woman with mixed results.
author: William Messner-Loebs

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue mini-series by Brian Michael Bendis and Alan Davis set in the aftermath of Siege, following Steve Rogers, Tony Stark, and Thor as they are stranded in the Nine Realms and must repair their fractured friendships before reuniting as heroes.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Fabian Nicieza's six-issue limited series focuses on Songbird's pivotal role in a confrontation between the Avengers and Thunderbolts, providing character-rich examination of redemption and institutional trust during the Disassembled era.
author: Kurt Busiek

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's penultimate arc on New Avengers and Avengers, an eight-month time-jump forward revealing the consequences of the Illuminati's incursion battles as the Marvel Universe hurtles toward Secret Wars; some of Hickman's most complex and emotionally devastating work.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Katy Farina's graphic novel adaptations of Ann M. Martin's spin-off series focusing on Karen Brewer, stepsister of BSC member Kristy, aimed at a slightly younger audience than the main series. Bright, cheerful adaptations that capture the spirit of the original books.
author: Ann M. Martin

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's official comics continuation of the Back to the Future franchise, featuring stories set before, during, and after the film trilogy by writers including Bob Gale and John Barber. A solid extension of the beloved property that fills in gaps in the films' timeline.
author: Bob Gale, John Barber

subject: series
synopsis: Christian Ward's 2023 DC Black Label series exploring a hidden city of criminals deep beneath Gotham — a beautifully surreal, visually extraordinary horror adventure that showcases Ward's painted art style working at full psychedelic intensity.
author: Christian Ward

subject: series
synopsis: Trade reprints of late-1980s and 1990s Detective Comics, Alan Grant, John Wagner and Norm Breyfogle's Batman with Aparo and Milligan stories.
author: Alan Grant, Peter Milligan

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's 2008 Marvel mini for the Japanese government super-team Big Hero 6, before the Disney film.

subject: series
synopsis: An Action Lab spinoff series expanding on a character from Vampblade, continuing the pulpy exploitation-horror action of that universe with a new lead.
author: Shawn Gabborin

subject: series
synopsis: Kelly Thompson and Meredith McClaren's Image fantasy noir: two detectives of the Black Cloak investigate a murder in a city of magic.
author: Kelly Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: The DC reprint series collected Jack Kirby and Joe Simon's original horror anthology from Prize Comics, presenting their pre-Code horror work with its striking splash pages and twist endings intact. The Kirby/Simon collaboration at its most viscerally pulpy and inventive.
author: Jack Kirby

subject: series
synopsis: David Liss's Black Panther (2011-2012): powerless T'Challa protects Hell's Kitchen and fights the Kingpin in a street-level noir.
author: David Liss

subject: series
synopsis: DC's New 52 reboot of the classic war comics property, featuring a modern covert military team with enhanced tech. A short-lived New 52 title that struggled to distinguish itself in the crowded marketplace.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Nakatani Nio's acclaimed yuri manga following Yuu Koito, a girl who can't understand romantic feelings, and Touko Nanami, a seemingly perfect student body president who falls for Yuu precisely because she makes no demands of her. A psychologically precise and deeply empathetic romance that approaches its subject matter with more sophistication than almost any manga of its era.
author: Nakatani Nio

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Diana's underground zine that became the center of a landmark First Amendment legal case when Diana became the first American artist convicted of obscenity for his own artwork in 1994. The crude horror and transgressive content was deliberately provocative, and the legal battle made it a cause celebre for free speech advocates.
author: Mike Diana

subject: series
synopsis: A comedy manga by Kyosuke Arai centering on a protagonist with an obsessive fixation on breasts, following the ecchi comedy genre conventions of its era. Fan-service heavy content that prioritizes its comedic premise over character depth.
author: Kyosuke Arai

subject: series
synopsis: Osamu Tezuka's monumental eight-volume manga biography of Siddhartha Gautama, mixing historical epic with invented characters and Tezuka's characteristic blending of pathos, comedy, and philosophical depth; one of the God of Manga's greatest achievements.
author: Osamu Tezuka

subject: series
synopsis: The Comic Book Legal Defense Fund's anthology series produced to raise money and awareness for free speech in comics, featuring creator-donated stories in support of the organization's work defending comics against censorship.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Trina Robbins's 1987 Eclipse comic about twin teen sisters in California, a revival of girls' fashion-and-romance comics.

subject: series
synopsis: CLAMP's beloved magical girl manga following Sakura Kinomoto as she accidentally releases the magical Clow Cards and must capture them all to prevent disaster. One of the most warmly beloved magical girl manga of all time — gentle, emotionally nuanced, beautifully drawn, and remarkably progressive in its depiction of love across gender and age.
author: CLAMP

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Gonick's long-running educational comics series presenting world history from the Big Bang through the 20th century with wit, genuine scholarship, and comedic craft. One of the finest educational comics ever created.
author: Larry Gonick

subject: series
synopsis: The second Sam and Twitch series (2003-2004): the Spawn-universe NYPD detectives in supernatural crime cases.

subject: series
synopsis: Dave Sim's surreal continuation exploring Cerebus in nightmarish scenarios.
author: Dave Sim

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's series starring Miles Morales, Kamala Khan, and Sam Alexander forming a youth-led team that breaks from the Avengers, focused on social justice themes and optimistic heroism.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Aspen Comics' urban fantasy series following a Las Vegas magician who discovers real magic exists when he is swept into an ancient conflict between magical forces, featuring the slick art style and action-focused storytelling typical of Aspen's output.
author: Vince Hernandez

subject: series
synopsis: A supernatural horror series about a disgraced cop returning to her New England hometown to confront dark magical forces.
author: Caitlin Kittredge

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Kelley Jones's Dark Horse miniseries chronicles the origin of Thoth-Amon, Conan's great sorcerous nemesis, tracing his rise from desperate thief to master of black magic. A dark fantasy prequel within Robert E. Howard's Hyborian world.
author: Kurt Busiek

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Epic Collection reprints of Dark Horse's Conan, Busiek, Truman, Nord and Giorello adapting Robert E. Howard.
author: Robert E. Howard, Timothy Truman

subject: series
synopsis: Titan Comics' Conan the Barbarian series featuring the Cimmerian warrior in sword-and-sorcery adventures. Battle of the Black Stone arc.

subject: series
synopsis: A light digital-first comedy mystery from Monkeybrain Comics following Copernicus Jones, a robot detective solving cases in a retro-futurist world, blending noir tropes with slapstick humor.
author: Matt D. Wilson

subject: series
synopsis: The 4-issue Countdown crossover pitting multiversal variants of DC heroes against each other in gladiatorial combat organized by Monarch. The concept is more interesting than the execution, which defaults to action spectacle over the character drama the premise implies.
author: Keith Champagne

subject: series
synopsis: Sammy Harkham's long-running self-published anthology showcasing his own literary comics work alongside curated contributions from notable alternative cartoonists. A cornerstone of the small-press scene, featuring Harkham's acclaimed 'Poor Sailor' and 'Crickets' serial narratives.
author: Sammy Harkham

subject: series
synopsis: A Europe Comics fantasy epic exploring religious conflict and noble quests across mythical lands.

subject: series
synopsis: Terry LaBan's autobiographical and fiction comics series from Fantagraphics, blending personal observation with pop culture satire. Part of the early 1990s alternative comics scene that found a home at Fantagraphics alongside similar slice-of-life and humor-driven titles.
author: Terry LaBan

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's acclaimed horror event series in which a corrupted version of the Anti-Life Equation spreads via digital technology, transforming DC's heroes into zombies and forcing the survivors to face an apocalyptic world with no clean answers.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2020 anthology collects short stories from across the publisher's stable of characters and creative teams, functioning as a sampler of the line's range and talent. Uneven as all anthologies are, but showcases some of DC's best short-form work from a transitional editorial period.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Wood and Rebekah Isaacs' DV8 miniseries drops the team onto a primitive world where they become gods to superstitious locals — a pointed examination of power, colonialism, and what these people do when no one's watching.
author: Brian Wood

subject: series
synopsis: Jan Strnad and Dennis Fujitake's eight-issue Fantagraphics sci-fi series about Dalgoda, a gentle duck-billed alien ambassador who crash-lands on Earth and discovers that humanity is not the civilized species the universe expected. A warmly humane alien-visitor story that found a devoted following among alternative comics readers of the mid-1980s.
author: Jan Strnad

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology series with three separate arcs by different creative teams, leading with Lee Weeks's beautiful, self-contained story about Daredevil navigating a blizzard to deliver medicine across New York. Weeks's arc in particular showcased exceptional craft.
author: Lee Weeks

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinite Comic pairing Daredevil and the Punisher in an interconnected crime thriller set in New York's criminal underworld, with each issue told simultaneously from both heroes' perspectives.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinite Comic bridging Daredevil's relocation to San Francisco, following Matt Murdock on a cross-country road trip that tests his identity as both man and devil.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: A mature-readers Red Band miniseries pushing Daredevil into brutal, uncompromising territory with graphic violence and dark themes, Marvel's attempt to recapture the MAX-era intensity for the Man Without Fear.

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule's acclaimed run launches here as a newly secret-identity-restored Matt Murdock mentors a new Daredevil while confronting the Hand and navigating a legally and morally complex world.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel/Timely's golden-age anthology from 1940–1942 featuring a rotating roster of early masked heroes — the Fiery Mask, Mister E, the Phantom Reporter — in short adventure strips. An important historical artifact of Marvel's earliest publishing experiments before the superhero template was fully established.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's superhero team series featuring a group tasked with protecting the universe in the far future, part of the shared Marvel UK universe of the early 1990s. Competent but not enduring.
author: Dan Abnett

subject: series
synopsis: Fabian Nicieza and Joe Madureira's 1993 four-issue limited series — Deadpool's first solo story — sending the Merc with a Mouth on a globe-trotting chase that established his fast-talking, self-aware persona and his complicated history with Weapon X. The origin point of the character's enormous later popularity.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinite Comic murder mystery featuring Deadpool investigating the deaths of comedy-themed Marvel characters, blending the Merc with a Mouth's irreverent humor with classic whodunit structure.
author: Joshua Corin

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's meta horror-comedy concluding the 'Deadpool Killogy,' in which Deadpool from the main Marvel universe must prevent a murderous version of himself from killing all alternate Deadpools across the multiverse. A self-aware, enjoyably ridiculous exercise in Deadpool's fourth-wall-breaking premise.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule and Steve McNiven's prestige miniseries depicting the canonical death of Logan after losing his healing factor, featuring painted art and a dignified, emotional conclusion to his story.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: The 1993 Valiant/Image crossover event, infamous for delays and its role in the speculator crash.

subject: series
synopsis: A 2002 Image science-horror series in which Earth and Hell edge toward war as the Devil seeks to claim Earth through his son.
author: Douglass D. Barre, Jacob Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Howard Chaykin's Die Hard prequel follows a young John McClane as a cop in 1970s New York City, building his character before the events of the film franchise.
author: Howard Chaykin

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's anthology comics featuring the classic Disney Afternoon animated characters — DuckTales, Darkwing Duck, TaleSpin, and Rescue Rangers — in new stories capturing the feel of the beloved 1990s animated block. A nostalgic treat for fans of the original shows.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Comics continuing the adventures of Drake Mallard — the terror that flaps in the night — across new cases in St. Canard.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Comics based on the Disney Channel animated series about a magical princess from another dimension attending school on Earth.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinite Comic crossover pitting Doctor Strange's mystic arts against the Punisher's brutal street-level warfare, as an unlikely alliance faces a threat that bridges both their worlds.

subject: series
synopsis: A Doctor Who anthology series presenting standalone ghost and supernatural horror stories. Features various Doctors encountering paranormal threats and eerie phenomena across time.
author: George Mann

subject: series
synopsis: The Twelfth Doctor (Peter Capaldi) faces alien threats, moral dilemmas, and cosmic conspiracies in this ongoing comic series from Titan Comics. Set during the TV series era, it captures the Doctor's brooding intelligence and dry wit alongside companion Clara and others.
author: Colin Bell, Robbie Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Anthology collecting stories featuring both Donald Duck and Mickey Mouse in shared adventures.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A Dracula-centric tie-in exploring the vampire king's involvement in the Blood Hunt event.
author: Danny Lore, Cavan Scott

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' superheroine series featuring Dragonfly, part of their line of female-led superhero comics in the mid-1980s that would feed into the FemForce team title.
author: Rik Levins, Wes Covington

subject: series
synopsis: A collected volume of Drawing Blood, a semi-autobiographical story about a teenage Ninja Turtles creator navigating the brutal comics industry and personal trauma.
author: David Avallone

subject: series
synopsis: Keith Giffen's miniseries reimagines Drax as a brutal, brain-damaged killing machine reborn in rural Alaska, establishing the gritty foundation that would lead into Annihilation.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: Ivan Brandon and Nic Klein's space western about a crashed pilot trying to survive on a hostile colonial frontier planet. Klein's painted art is gorgeous; the frontier atmosphere is well-realized.
author: Ivan Brandon

subject: series
synopsis: Stephen Graham Jones and Davide Gianfelice's sci-fi thriller follows Indigenous time travelers sent back to 1493 to assassinate Christopher Columbus — a dark, charged exploration of colonialism and its consequences.
author: Stephen Graham Jones

subject: series
synopsis: A Vertigo mystery series about a former child star turned cop investigating bizarre murders in a small town.
author: Tim Seeley

subject: series
synopsis: Ben Raab's 2001 four-issue Excalibur mini: Captain Britain and Meggan's new life as rulers in Otherworld.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Collected Excalibur stories showcasing the team's diverse adventures.
author: Chris Claremont, Scott Lobdell

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Davis's alternate-future story presents a reconciliation of the Fantastic Four in a Silver Age-inflected far future, drawn with Davis's signature clean elegance and characteristic optimism.
author: Alan Davis

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont and Jon Bogdanove's Marvel miniseries pits the two teams against each other after revelations about Reed Richards's possible role in Galactus's survival, with Doctor Doom manipulating events while offering to cure a dying Kitty Pryde. A character-driven clash of loyalties.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: The Dark Horse manga adaptation of Gen Urobuchi's Fate/Zero light novel prequel to Fate/stay night, depicting the brutal Fourth Holy Grail War through the perspective of adult Masters who understand what's at stake. A darker, more politically complex entry in the Fate mythology.
author: Gen Urobuchi (story)

subject: series
synopsis: Pin-up art portfolios featuring the female heroes of AC Comics' FemForce, showcasing the cheesecake art style central to AC Comics' brand identity during the late 1980s and 1990s.

subject: series
synopsis: Tatsuki Fujimoto's pre-Chainsaw Man manga following Agni, a 'blessed' human who can regenerate from anything, seeking revenge across a frozen post-apocalyptic world while being perpetually on fire. Ferociously original and deliberately uncomfortable, Fire Punch showcases Fujimoto's radical storytelling instincts in rough, brilliant form.
author: Tatsuki Fujimoto

subject: series
synopsis: Joss Whedon and Greg Pak's canonical Firefly continuation follows the crew of Serenity in new adventures across the 'verse, maintaining the show's beloved tone of found-family Western sci-fi.
author: Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's comprehensive collection of Lynn Johnston's beloved newspaper strip, which ran from 1979 to 2008 and followed the Patterson family through real-time aging and genuine life events including birth, adolescence, marriage, and loss. Johnston's willingness to let her characters actually grow older and face authentic emotional challenges made the strip a landmark in comics storytelling.
author: Lynn Johnston

subject: series
synopsis: Alternate version of the Death in the Family story where Jason Todd survives.
author: J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinity Comic companion to Jonathan Hickman's G.O.D.S. series, exploring the conflict between the forces of Nature and Technology in Marvel's cosmic hierarchy in vertical format.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Sean Mackiewicz and Niko Walter's Image Comics series about a couple caught between Mexican cartels and a supernatural force animating the dead in rural Mexico — a horror-western hybrid with genuine tension and real human stakes at its center.
author: Sean Mackiewicz

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's DC crossover event involving the Source Wall and the New Gods, generally considered one of the weaker DC crossover events that failed to justify its existence or live up to the grand Kirby mythology it drew on.
author: John Byrne

subject: series
synopsis: The Geomancer is a recurring role in the Valiant Comics universe — the human defender who channels the spirit of the Earth, connected to the Eternal Warrior across centuries. Multiple Valiant characters have held the title across different eras and storylines.
author: Maurice Fontenot

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first vertical Infinity Comic starring Kushala, the 19th-century Apache shaman Ghost Rider, exploring her unique perspective as a Spirit of Vengeance across historical and supernatural settings.
author: Taboo, B. Earl
artist: Guillermo Sanna, Vanesa R. Del Rey

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire and Andrea Sorrentino's horror mystery: a reclusive young man in the city and a priest in a small town are bound to a sinister black barn that appears through time.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Kaori Yuki's gothic Victorian manga following Cain Hargreaves, an earl with a tragic past who investigates crimes connected to a shadowy organization called Delilah, accompanied by his butler Riff and half-sister Mary Weather. Yuki's lavish gothic art style and taste for melodrama made this a standout of the 1990s Japanese gothic comics scene.
author: Kaori Yuki

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Phil Winslade's 1995 Vertigo series following an ordinary woman who discovers she's actually a goddess and must confront supernatural forces that have shaped her life. An early Ennis Vertigo project showing the mix of dark humor and genuine emotional engagement that characterized his best work.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Universe reference guides and sourcebooks for Fred Perry's Gold Digger action-fantasy series, providing in-universe encyclopedic information about characters, locations, and lore.
author: Fred Perry

subject: series
synopsis: Cullen Bunn's series following several Green Lanterns stranded in a distant and ancient part of the universe, having to survive without their standard backup. An isolated survival story with interesting mythology.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: DC's comics adaptation of the 2011 Green Lantern: The Animated Series, featuring Hal Jordan and Kilowog in the animated series' distinctive visual style. A well-produced all-ages companion to the short-lived but critically appreciated animated series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's archival collection of Hal Jordan's earliest Green Lantern stories from the 1960s, presenting Gil Kane's foundational art and the John Broome plots that established the entire GL mythology. Essential historical reading for understanding how the Silver Age reinvented the Golden Age concept.
author: John Broome

subject: series
synopsis: DC's anthology series focusing on Green Lanterns beyond Hal Jordan and Guy Gardner, showcasing the diverse alien membership of the Corps in standalone stories. A solid way to expand the mythology between regular issues.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's revival of the classic First Comics character created by John Ostrander and Tim Truman — Grimjack, a mercenary operating in Cynosure, a nexus city where all dimensions intersect. Truman returns to the character he co-created.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Sergio Aragones and Mark Evanier's long-running comedy follows Groo, a dim-witted, cheese-dip-obsessed barbarian whose peerless swordsmanship is matched only by his genius for accidentally destroying everything around him. A satirical sword-and-sorcery farce.
author: Sergio Aragonés

subject: series
synopsis: Kenichi Sonoda's beloved manga about Bean Bandit and Rally Vincent, Chicago bounty hunters who specialize in gun-related crimes, featuring meticulous firearms accuracy, high-speed car chases, and irresistible lead chemistry. A must-read for action-manga fans.
author: Kenichi Sonoda

subject: series
synopsis: A comics adaptation of H.P. Lovecraft's classic cosmic horror story about the monstrous Whateley family and the terrible entity they summon in the rural New England town of Dunwich. A faithful adaptation of one of Lovecraft's most visceral and disturbing tales.

subject: series
synopsis: Fabian Nicieza's 2003 Hawkeye ongoing: Clint Barton as a down-on-his-luck hero in Los Angeles, cancelled after eight issues.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: A psychological horror thriller from Monkeybrain Comics set inside the mind of a serial killer, where the residents of a mental landscape must survive as dark secrets unravel.
author: Ryan K. Lindsay

subject: series
synopsis: Max Bemis and Eryk Donovan's Vault Comics series about Joe, a hitman in the afterlife who must kill evil souls to earn his way to heaven after a life of violence. A redemption narrative with genuine moral weight and Donovan's striking visual energy.
author: Max Bemis

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries set during World War II following a team of soldiers who encounter supernatural and demonic forces on the battlefield, connecting to the Ghost Rider legacy in Marvel's wartime era.
author: Phillip Kennedy Johnson

subject: series
synopsis: A miniseries set in the Xavier Institute following the student team called the Hellions, exploring life among mutant youth during the New X-Men era. Part of Grant Morrison's broader X-Men revamp.
author: Nunzio DeFilippis

subject: series
synopsis: Natsume Ono's quiet, melancholic manga about a shy, ineffectual ronin who becomes entangled with a small gang of morally ambiguous kidnappers for hire in Edo-period Japan. Distinguished by Ono's scratchy, intimate art style and her interest in character psychology over action — one of the most literary historical manga of its era.
author: Natsume Ono

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel Masterworks reprints of Steve Gerber's legendary Howard the Duck, one of the most satirically sharp and culturally subversive comics Marvel ever published, following the cigar-chomping duck trapped in a world he never made.
author: Steve Gerber

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's legendary twelve-year Hulk run collected here represents the definitive treatment of Bruce Banner, blending psychology, humor, and superhero drama in ways that permanently elevated the character.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and Ivan Reis' supernatural noir is set in a hidden city street connecting the real world to the underworld, where predatory monsters live alongside the recently deceased.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid's companion series to Irredeemable follows super-villain Max Damage who, horrified by the Plutonian's rampage, decides to become a genuine hero — darkly comic redemption story in a world gone wrong.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: An Action Lab Entertainment spy-action series following a teenage girl who is recruited into an elite international assassin organization after her father's death, blending YA adventure with globe-trotting action.
author: Dave Dwonch

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Peter Krause's digital-to-print series about a veteran superhero forced to work with his arrogant, fame-obsessed former sidekick — a sharp satire of celebrity culture, social media, and the superhero business. Waid's facility with character dynamics made this one of his most purely entertaining creator-owned works.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue limited series pairing the martial-arts heroes Iron Fist and Wolverine in a fast-paced action-adventure with ties to the criminal underworld.

subject: series
synopsis: The comics adaptation of Jim Butcher's second Dresden Files novel, following Chicago wizard-detective Harry Dresden investigating a series of werewolf killings during a full moon. A competent adaptation of the popular urban fantasy novel series.
author: Mark Powers (adapted)

subject: series
synopsis: Annual graphic-novel horror anthologies curated by John Carpenter, short Halloween tales by rotating creators.
author: David J. Schow, Duane Swierczynski

subject: series
synopsis: Collected/director's cut edition of Jhonen Vasquez's Johnny the Homicidal Maniac with restored content.
author: Jhonen Vasquez

subject: series
synopsis: A classic Atlas/Marvel horror and sci-fi anthology title from the 1950s featuring strange tales and twist endings, an important piece of pre-superhero Marvel history and a key influence on the later monster comics.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Milligan's New 52 launch gathering DC's mystical heroes (John Constantine, Zatanna, Deadman, Swamp Thing) into a team to fight magical threats, later improved by Jeff Lemire's run.
author: Peter Milligan

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Williamson's 2017 DC event series pitting the Justice League against the Suicide Squad in an escalating conflict that reveals a greater threat behind the scenes. A Rebirth-era event executed with clean superhero clarity.
author: Joshua Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: Rodney Barnes and Jason Shawn Alexander's vampire horror: a Baltimore detective returns home to Philadelphia to find his murdered father risen and a vampire army led by John Adams.
author: Rodney Barnes

subject: series
synopsis: Fantasy action series from Mad Cave Studios following angelic warriors and archangels in a world where biblical mythology shapes epic conflict between heaven and hell.
author: Mark London

subject: series
synopsis: A four-issue limited series set during the Magneto-ruled Genosha period, examining the Master of Magnetism's attempts to govern his mutant nation while navigating political intrigue and confrontations with his former allies.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Dingess and Matthew Roberts' horror-western about Lewis and Clark's expedition encountering monsters and ancient evils across the American frontier. Roberts' creature designs are spectacular; the colonial horror subtext is pointed.
author: Chris Dingess

subject: series
synopsis: André Franquin's beloved Belgian comics creation — the lovable spotted jungle creature with an impossibly long tail — in collected adventures that showcase Franquin's extraordinary facility for physical comedy and warm character work.
author: André Franquin

subject: series
synopsis: Trade paperback adaptations of the 1994 Iron Man animated series, bringing the Saturday morning cartoon's adventures into comics form for all-ages readers.
author: Ron Friedman, Eric Fein

subject: series
synopsis: A trade paperback adaptation of the 1994 Fantastic Four animated series, collecting comics based on the Saturday morning cartoon and bringing the animated adventures into the printed page format.
author: Joey Cavalieri, Ron Friedman

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's adaptation of Homer's Iliad in comic form, part of the Illustrated line bringing classical literature to sequential art. Roy Thomas's script treatment respects the source material while making it accessible.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
